title: SCIM: safe deprovisioning heuristics, role-mapping, and admin reconciliation playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Reduce customer-facing user/account deletions from SCIM deprovisioning while keeping automated flows reliable and auditable. Deliver a defensible pipeline that: 1) ensures provisioning operations are idempotent and resumable, 2) provides a quarantined ‘soft-delete’ path with configurable TTL and admin reconciliation tooling, 3) maps identity provider roles/groups to RBAC v2 constructs safely, and 4) enriches audit logs and metrics for postmortem and SLO tracking.

Scope and approach:
- Implement a tombstone/soft-delete layer upstream of final deletion. SCIM deprovision requests set user/group state to QUARANTINED with a tombstone timestamp and metadata (scim_request_id, idp_origin, incoming_payload_sha256, retry_count). Final hard-delete occurs only after TTL expiry and passing safety checks.
- Idempotency keys: persist a scim_request_id per incoming request and make reconcile/deprovision operations idempotent by skipping already-applied actions and returning stable results.
- Retry and backoff policy: use exponential backoff with full-jitter for automated SCIM retry attempts, bounded max attempts, and probabilistic gating when IDP rate limits or tenant error rates exceed thresholds. Integrate with lease/circuit-breaker (ENG-36789) to avoid cascading failures.
- Orphan detection: run a daily reconcile for accounts that have been QUARANTINED longer than grace window and compare against activity, tokens, and last-login signals before final removal. Flag high-risk deletions for manual approval when certain heuristics match (SAML-linked service accounts, active API keys, recent billing events).
- RBAC v2 role-group mapping: add a verified mapping table that translates IDP groups -> RBAC roles -> internal group IDs. Changes to mapping must be auditable and require two-step approval in admin console for tenants with >= enterprise tier.
- Admin reconciliation UI & API: build console view showing quarantine queue, filters (age, tenant, role, risk score), and actions (undelete/restore, extend TTL, request escalation, force-delete). Expose programmatic endpoints for solutions engineers to perform bulk restores with audit annotations.
- Audit & observability: enrich every state transition with scim_request_id, actor, evidence links (GitHub PR, support ticket), and reason. Emit metrics: scim_deprovision_attempts, scim_deprovision_success, scim_deprovision_failures_by_reason, quarantine_count, reconciliation_lag_seconds, scim_retry_attempts. Add dashboard and alert when quarantine_count growth rate > 5%/day for a tenant.
- Tests and safety nets: integration tests against a SCIM sandbox with simulated rate limits and flaky responses, chaos tests that exercise partial failures during group syncs, and an automated canary rollout for the new flow.

Non-goals: automatic re-provisioning of external IDP users, changes to SCIM schema beyond adding metadata fields, or implementing tenant billing reversions as part of restore.

Runbook / operational notes: provide a runbook for oncall describing how to identify erroneous mass-deprovision events, steps to pause reconciler, how to extend TTLs, and emergency restore procedures. Link to runbook in links.
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent SCIM reconciler implemented: repeated delivery of same scim_request_id is safe and does not cause multiple deletes.
Soft-delete (QUARANTINED) state added with configurable TTL; default 30d for non-enterprise tenants, 7d for enterprise when requested.
Admin console shows quarantine queue with restore/extend/force-delete actions and records audit annotations for each action.
Audit logs include scim_request_id, idp_origin, incoming_payload_sha256, and operator annotations for all transitions.
Metrics and a Grafana dashboard created for deprovision health; alert when quarantine_count growth rate exceeds threshold.
Automated integration tests and a canary rollout plan exist and have been executed in staging with failure scenarios covered.
